project.name: bioFM
project.description: The code half of the bioFM workspace: two independent Python packages. `chipsim` is an in-silico lung-on-a-chip exposure and barrier-response pipeline (ingest → harmonize → encoders → heads → transport → occupancy → surface → uncertainty → eval → acquire) built on RDKit, pandas and DVC, with a record-content guard and a `chipsim` CLI. `perturb-eval` is an agentic evaluation harness that pits contextual Bayesian optimization against evolutionary hyperparameter tuning on perturb-seq mean-squared-difference benchmarks, with a Modal-based remote execution layer. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: bayesian.py
nodes.summary: Bayesian recommender mapping a probe signature to the MAP configuration under a FLOPs budget, using a per-config Gaussian likelihood and a configurable size-favouring prior computed in log space.
nodes.languageNotes: Posterior is accumulated in log space with a diagonal covariance — deliberately simple because the calibration set is at most ~100 tasks over 4-d signatures.

nodes.name: Recommendation
nodes.summary: Frozen result of a recommendation: the chosen Config, its log posterior, the per-config log likelihoods, the full ranking, the budget applied and how many tasks the model was fit on.

nodes.name: BayesianRecommender
nodes.summary: Fits per-configuration Gaussian means and variances from labelled probe signatures, then returns the budget-feasible config maximising log prior plus log likelihood.

nodes.name: calibration.py
nodes.summary: Fits the TDI coefficients from logged runs with a small ridge regression, the calibration step that turns raw orchestration metrics into a single difficulty index.
nodes.languageNotes: Ridge rather than OLS specifically because the calibration set is small — the penalty keeps the four coefficients from blowing up on N of order tens.

nodes.name: TDICoeffs
nodes.summary: Frozen four-coefficient carrier (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) weighting the TDI terms, with a dict view for serialisation.

nodes.name: fit_tdi_coefficients
nodes.summary: Builds the design matrix from labelled RunTraces (delta-ACE, delta mean confidence, winner flip rate) and solves the ridge normal equations for the TDI coefficients.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: The metric library behind the evaluation layer — ACE, CSD, delta-ACE, delta-confidence, winner flip rate, critique-severity star and the composite TDI — all pure functions over RoundTrace/RunTrace.
nodes.languageNotes: Softmax entropy is computed with the log-sum-exp trick and variance with ddof=0, so the metrics stay numerically stable without pulling in SciPy.

nodes.name: ace
nodes.summary: Agent Confidence Entropy: the temperature-scaled softmax entropy of a round's agent confidences, the core disagreement signal.

nodes.name: ace_norm
nodes.summary: ACE normalised by log(n_agents) so rounds with different agent counts are comparable.

nodes.name: ace_d
nodes.summary: Discrete variant of ACE computed over a distribution derived from the raw confidences without temperature scaling.

nodes.name: critique_severity_dispersion
nodes.summary: Spread of critique severities within a round — how unevenly the agents criticised each other.

nodes.name: critique_severity_max
nodes.summary: The single harshest critique severity observed in a round.

nodes.name: critique_severity_star
nodes.summary: The CST statistic combining critique severity magnitude and concentration into one round-level score.

nodes.name: _flatten_critiques
nodes.summary: Flattens the N x (N-1) critique-severity matrix into a single ordered sequence, skipping the self-critique diagonal.

nodes.name: round_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes the full RoundMetrics record (ACE, normalised ACE, confidence stats, CSD, winner index, consensus score) for one RoundTrace.

nodes.name: delta_ace
nodes.summary: Change in ACE from the first to the last round — whether the agents converged or diverged in confidence.

nodes.name: delta_mean_confidence
nodes.summary: Change in mean agent confidence across the run.

nodes.name: winner_flip_rate
nodes.summary: Fraction of round transitions in which the winning agent changed — a direct instability signal.

nodes.name: tdi
nodes.summary: Task Difficulty Index: the calibrated linear combination of delta-ACE, delta-confidence, winner flip rate and severity into one scalar.

nodes.name: tdi2
nodes.summary: Second-order TDI variant adding pairwise interaction terms on top of the linear coefficients.

nodes.name: run_metrics
nodes.summary: Assembles the RunMetrics record for a whole RunTrace: per-round metrics plus the run-level deltas and TDI.

nodes.name: journal.py
nodes.summary: Append-only run journal (build-plan S12) that snapshots every config file, resolved package versions, environment and seed into a digest-sealed manifest per run, writes the outcome last, and verifies records on read to detect after-the-fact tampering.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of os-level fd operations (O_NOFOLLOW-style object verification, hard-link and FIFO refusal) to defend config snapshotting against symlink and path-traversal tricks.

nodes.name: _recorded_argv
nodes.summary: Normalizes argv for recording: argv[0] reduced to its basename so absolute interpreter paths are not leaked, the tail kept verbatim.

nodes.name: manifest_digest
nodes.summary: Computes the canonical sha256 digest of a run manifest used to seal and later verify the record.

nodes.name: source_root
nodes.summary: Returns the non-overridable source tree root of the installed chipsim package, used to anchor provenance.

nodes.name: _package_versions
nodes.summary: Collects resolved versions of pinned dependencies (e.g. pyarrow, rdkit) so a record can show two runs used the same computation stack.

nodes.name: _resolve_seed
nodes.summary: Resolves the run seed with precedence CHIPSIM_SEED over configs/env.yaml:seed and records which source won, refusing unparseable configs rather than reporting the seed as unset.

nodes.name: _coerce_seed
nodes.summary: Strictly validates a seed value as an integer, refusing booleans, floats and underscored strings instead of recording junk.

nodes.name: _environment
nodes.summary: Captures platform, interpreter, journal relocation and raw seed environment variables by value for the run manifest.

nodes.name: _validate_run_id
nodes.summary: Rejects run ids that could traverse outside the journal directory.

nodes.name: _config_sources
nodes.summary: Walks the configs boundary at any depth (.yaml and .yml), following in-project symlinked directories while bounding enumeration and refusing escapes, cycles and diamonds.

nodes.name: _configs_boundary
nodes.summary: The single canonical boundary every reader of configs/ must use; resolves the real configs directory and refuses one that is itself a symlink out of the tree or to the project root.

nodes.name: _refuse_escaping_config
nodes.summary: Raises ConfigIntegrityError for a config whose real path lies outside the configs boundary.

nodes.name: _open_verified_config
nodes.summary: Opens a config for snapshotting verified as an object rather than a name, refusing hard links, FIFOs and broken symlinks so the bytes copied are the bytes verified.

nodes.name: start_run
nodes.summary: Opens a new run directory, snapshots every config by copy, records argv/environment/versions/seed and writes the digest-sealed manifest before any work begins; leaves no partial directory on failure.

nodes.name: read_manifest
nodes.summary: Verifies a run record (manifest digest, location binding, config snapshot) and returns the manifest, raising ManifestVerificationError on tampering.

nodes.name: _verify_config_snapshot

nodes.name: outcome_digest
nodes.summary: Computes the digest that binds an outcome record to its run manifest.

nodes.name: finish_run

nodes.name: read_outcome
nodes.summary: Verifies and returns a run's outcome or None if no completion was recorded, detecting forged, copied or unbound outcomes.

nodes.name: record_invocation
nodes.summary: Writes a lightweight, non-overwriting invocation record (argv and environment, no config digest) for human commands like panel-seal that are not ETL runs.

nodes.name: JournalError
nodes.summary: Base exception for all run-journal failures.

nodes.name: ConfigIntegrityError
nodes.summary: Raised when a config cannot be snapshotted safely (escaping symlink, hard link, FIFO, unparseable seed source).

nodes.name: ManifestVerificationError
nodes.summary: Raised when a run manifest or its config snapshot fails verification on read.

nodes.name: confidence.py

layers.name: Chipsim Pipeline Core
layers.description: The chipsim package: the pipeline.py ETL CLI and journal.py run recorder, ingest (DrugBank snapshot) and harmonize (identity canonicalization, P-gp labels, adjudication, rosters, provenance contracts), the new M1 transport core (theta/prior containers, sourcing-worksheet validator, two-compartment ODE, MAP fit), the LBM audit power/budget/series modules, the output-root write guard, the aviary sandbox surface, and the eval provenance block; acquire/encoders/heads/occupancy/surface/uncertainty remain empty stage markers.

layers.name: Perturb-Eval Core Library
layers.description: The importable perturb_eval package (Poetry src-layout): typed protocols, metrics, calibration, probes, Bayesian recommendation, backbones and optimizers, the data package (Adamson/Norman loaders, construct parser, label contract, subsampling, HVG), OpenRouter and Anthropic LLM clients, the agentic lifecycle loop, and the experiments package with the v0.5/v0.6 sweep, pre-registered estimators and run provenance.

layers.name: Execution Drivers
layers.description: What actually launches work: the Modal apps and read-only Modal audits that run sweeps remotely, the local dry-run, analysis and figure-rendering scripts, the paper-number fillers and Zenodo/Figshare/OSF deposit scripts, the end-to-end example, the n8n DrugBank ETL workflow that shells out to python -m chipsim.pipeline, and the MassGen skill draft handlers, extractors, prompt and upstream patch. Import edges here are mostly absent from the graph (function-scoped Modal imports), so this is the execution surface, not dead code.

layers.name: Tests & Fixtures
layers.description: The pytest suites of both projects and the fixture corpus they read: chipsim tests over parsing, harmonization, adjudication, transport ODE/fit, M1 input contracts, audit power and sandbox readiness, backed by synthetic barrier-panel, roster, theta/prior, adjudication-CSV and DrugBank-snapshot fixtures; perturb_eval tests over metrics, optimizers, loaders, LLM clients, the lifecycle, Amendment-2 preregistration rules and manuscript-number pinning.

layers.name: Verification Guards
layers.description: Repository-level invariants rather than library behaviour: the authorship-overclaim honesty scan, fixture-leak and fixture-source scans, the scaffold/S6 absence and DVC-remote checks, the conftest meta-test, the n8n workflow export contract, the perturb-seq-eval bans on synthetic generators and on more than one lifecycle_runs.jsonl producer, plus the three GitHub Actions workflows (chipsim M1 lint/type/test, HACP link and Notion sync check, arXiv packaging) that enforce them on every push.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: bioFM is a workspace for biological foundation models, and its code half is two independent Python packages, each with its own pyproject.toml and uv.lock: chipsim, an in-silico lung-on-a-chip exposure and barrier-response pipeline, and perturb_eval, a perturb-seq agentic evaluation and Bayesian hyperparameter-tuning package. Start with README.md for the layout, then CLAUDE.md for the rules everything below is built to enforce. The main one is that no coding agent writes a biological number: every value is cited, derived or assumed, and a validator rejects anything unsourced. CONTEXT-MAP.md shows how the ChipSim context connects to the rest of the workspace.

tour.title: ChipSim Pipeline Entry Point
tour.description: pipeline.py is the chipsim CLI and has the largest fan-out of any code module. Its argparse subcommands run the ETL stages (fetch, hash-verify, parse, provenance tests, harmonize and worksheet steps) one after another, and the n8n workflow etl_drugbank.json calls those same stages through python -m chipsim.pipeline. The module README and CONTEXT.md glossary define the vocabulary used from here on: compound, curated chip, barrier panel and the M0 data spine.
tour.languageLesson: Python argparse subcommands, registered with add_subparsers and set_defaults(func=...), give one module several CLI verbs without a framework, so `python -m chipsim.pipeline <stage>` works the same way from a shell, from CI or from n8n.

tour.title: Journalled Runs and Write Guards
tour.description: Following imports out of pipeline.py, the first module the BFS reaches is journal.py, an append-only run journal. Each run snapshots every config file and the resolved package versions, so you can later reconstruct how any output was produced. The output-root guard only lets record-bearing writers write into declared untracked output roots. ADR 0001 explains why the journal deliberately does not record git state.

tour.title: The DrugBank Data Spine
tour.description: Every chipsim input starts as a pinned public DrugBank 4.2 snapshot. drugbank_snapshot.py fetches it, checks it against SHA256SUMS.json and parses it, and it has the highest fan-in of any chipsim source module. contracts.py enforces the ratified provenance contract on provenance.yaml (nine required keys, plus a rationale whenever the source commit changes), and sources.yaml records where every other external source came from. This is the first place the integrity model from Step 1 turns into code.

tour.title: Compound Identity and P-gp Labels
tour.description: ids.py uses RDKit to canonicalize compound identity (strip salts, neutralize, derive canonical keys), and so much of the harmonize layer depends on it that it ties drugbank_snapshot.py for the highest fan-in in chipsim. pgp_label.py joins compounds to barrier_panel.yaml, a transporter panel that only counts once a human has ratified and hash-sealed it, and assigns a three-way P-gp substrate label. Nothing at this layer infers a biological fact. It only joins data that was already sourced.

tour.title: Human Adjudication and Rosters
tour.description: When the data cannot settle a label, chipsim hands the decision to a person. adjudication.py writes a literature-review worksheet and loads the filled result back, refusing rows that lack evidence. pgp_adjudication.csv is that human-owned table, keyed by canonical InChIKey from Step 5. roster.py validates poc_compounds.yaml, the principal-owned proof-of-concept roster, which must hold 20 to 40 entries, each with a DOI. Together they mark the boundary between what code produces and what humans decide.

tour.title: M1 Transport Core and Sourcing
tour.description: The transport core holds the model: ode.py is a two-compartment (apical/basolateral) chip transport ODE, and fit.py fits its two free parameters, alpha and k_sink, by MAP estimation. theta.py and prior.py declare the parameter containers and refuse any fixed parameter or prior that lacks a citation or a stated assumption. sourcing.py checks the literature worksheet and rejects any filled row that is not cited, derived or assumed with the evidence each class requires. These three modules enforce the rule from Step 1 that unbacked data cannot be used.
tour.languageLesson: Frozen dataclasses (@dataclass(frozen=True)) combined with a validation function that raises on bad input give you 'parse, don't validate': once a Theta object exists, the rest of the code can rely on it being well-sourced.

tour.title: Audits and the Readiness Gate
tour.description: Before any GPU money is spent, power.py simulates statistical power and applies a halt rule, and budget.py re-projects total spend from measured throughput. The sandbox exposes the virtual lung membrane to agents as an aviary environment. readiness.py checks, artifact by artifact, whether the human-owned inputs from Steps 6-7 exist, and interpretability.py requires every prediction to report where each parameter came from. ADR 0003 records the power floor these audits enforce.

tour.title: ChipSim Tests, Honesty Scan, CI
tour.description: The test suite is where chipsim's guarantees are checked: test_fixtures.py has the highest fan-in in the graph, and test_m1_inputs.py checks the M1 input contracts from Step 7. honesty_scan.py scans provenance and journal text for authorship overclaims, catching wording that claims a human did something an agent did, or the reverse. The chipsim-m1-inputs workflow runs uv sync, ruff, ty and pytest on every change, so CI checks the same guarantees.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions: a workflow's `on: paths:` filter limits it to changes under one module, and its steps run in order, so a failing ruff or ty check stops the job before pytest starts.

tour.title: perturb_eval Entry and Thesis
tour.description: Now the second package. perturb_eval asks whether signals from a multi-agent debate (confidence entropy, critique severity) predict how hard a perturb-seq modelling task is, and whether that can steer hyperparameter tuning; THESIS.md states the pre-registered question. cli.py is a Typer app with three commands (preflight, calibrate, evaluate), and __main__.py makes `python -m perturb_eval` call the same app. From cli.py, the BFS reaches bayesian.py and probe.py first, then types.py and metrics.py.
tour.languageLesson: Typer builds a CLI from type-annotated function signatures: each @app.command() function becomes a subcommand, and its parameter annotations become validated options.

tour.title: Traces, Metrics, Probe, Recommender
tour.description: types.py is the most depended-on module in perturb_eval (fan-in 19). It defines the per-round and per-run debate traces that everything else reads and writes. metrics.py turns those traces into scores such as ACE and CSD; probe.py runs one cheap, shallow debate round to produce a difficulty signature; and calibration.py fits the coefficients that map that signature to a difficulty estimate. bayesian.py then recommends the MAP configuration for that signature under a FLOPs budget. Together these form preflight, calibrate and evaluate, the three commands from Step 10.

tour.title: The Agentic Lifecycle Loop
tour.description: loop.py has the largest fan-out in perturb_eval's library code. It runs several rounds of propose, execute, critique and refine across a pool of role agents: DataCurator, Literature, Architect, Trainer and Validator. proposal_schema.py validates each role's structured proposal with Pydantic; llm_agent_pool.py builds role prompts and parses the LLM replies; architect_dispatch.py turns the Architect's proposal into a concrete backbone configuration; validator_gate.py scores the trained model and decides whether it passes. The loop produces the traces typed in Step 11.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models validate untrusted LLM JSON at the boundary: model_validate raises a ValidationError on malformed proposals, so the rest of the loop handles only well-typed objects.

tour.title: Backbones, Optimizers, Real Data
tour.description: The lifecycle needs real models and real data. backbones/ provides the predictors the Architect selects, from a pure-numpy linear model up to a small scGPT-like transformer. contextual_gp.py is the Bayesian optimizer compared against CMA-ES and random search. label_contract.py maps perturbation labels to genes, and every alias it accepts must be backed by evidence. heldout.py trains one model per held-out task, selecting highly variable genes from training data only so no test information leaks in.

tour.title: Pre-registration and Sweep Provenance
tour.description: perturb_eval applies the same integrity model as chipsim. PREREGISTRATION.md fixes the hypotheses H1-H5 and the estimators before any data is seen, and preregistered.py implements exactly those estimators as pure functions. v05_sweep.py is the testable core of the sweep, with a spend guard and per-cell records; provenance.py writes provenance.json for each run; and app_v05.py is the budget-capped Modal A100 app that actually runs the sweep. Amendments to the plan are recorded in a separate ledger rather than edited in silently.

tour.title: From Artifacts to Paper
tour.description: The workflow ends with the manuscript. fill_v060_numbers.py computes every result value in the paper from the committed v0.6.0 artifacts, so no number is typed in by hand, and amendments_v060.json records each pre-registration amendment with the commit and date it was locked. paper.tex has the highest fan-in of any perturb_eval non-code file, and the arxiv-package workflow compiles and bundles it in CI. hacp-docs.yml applies the same CI discipline to the human review surface: an edit under docs/hacp that has not been mirrored to Notion fails the build.
